A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the BiAlign study despite the changed title and formatting. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations on language understanding, reasoning and coding tasks, together with controlled experiments and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, revised ablations, and additional demonstration-selection, reverse-KL, model-scaling and cross-task transfer experiments.

M1.justification: The core output-KL plus preference-ranking framework remains. However, Section 3.2 replaces random subset sampling with similarity-based grouping and sampling subsets containing different numbers of similar demonstrations. Appendix A.5 also introduces an evaluated reverse-KL adaptation.

E1.justification: CrossFit and the existing evaluation benchmarks, including the additional mathematical reasoning datasets, remain. Appendix A.9 adds MMLU as an alignment-training source for evaluation on BBH, extending source-task coverage beyond the CrossFit training scenarios in v2.

E2.justification: The main baseline set remains Vanilla, FT, C-Pretrain and Output-Align. v3 adds evaluated KATE, MMR and IDS comparisons with and without BiAlign on GSM8K (Table 8), and a reverse-KL Output-Align comparator (Table 9). In-Context Pretraining is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported training budget changes from 10 to 4 epochs; the reduced-budget control changes from 5 to 2 epochs. Evaluation expands from default demonstrations to prompt variants. v3 also adds Llama 3, Phi 3 and Qwen-2.5 configurations while dropping the Phi-1.5/Phi-2 experiment. These substantially revise and extend the experimental settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds selector-integration and reverse-KL tests, Qwen scale sweeps, preference-consistency analyses on three additional retained benchmarks, and MMLU-to-BBH transfer. The sampling ablation changes from random sampling versus varied subset sizes to similarity-based versus random sampling. Existing subset-count, source-diversity and case-study analyses are retained in the appendix.

E5.justification: v2 reports point estimates without repeated-evaluation information. v3 specifies three evaluations using different prompts and adds ± quantities throughout Table 1. This introduces limited uncertainty reporting, but the ± statistic is not defined and independent training runs or seeds are not specified.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised and supplemented. Table 1's BiAlign averages change from 30.2 to 31.0 with the 13B teacher and from 31.7 to 32.7 with the 70B teacher, under changed sampling, training and evaluation settings. New results include BBH scores of 43.3 versus 40.2 for BiAlign versus Output-Align after MMLU training (Table 13). These are not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The principal loss equations and uniform-prior Bayesian argument remain. However, v2's explicit mathematical definition of the alternative ranking loss, Equation 4, is removed; v3 describes a variant without rank() without specifying its full formula. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution and novelty claim about jointly aligning input preferences and output distributions remain. The introduction strengthens its quantitative headline from approximately 18% and 13% relative improvement on GSM8K and LogiQA to approximately 20% and 18%, respectively.

C2.justification: The ranking-loss discussion shifts from robustness across formulations to emphasizing the importance of rank-based alignment. v3 also argues for similarity-based sampling and adds an information-prioritization explanation in Appendix A.8. The computational-overhead limitation is unchanged and merely relocated.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 specifies Sentence-BERT representations, cosine similarity and an approximately equal split between similarity groups. The epoch budget is revised, while existing software, hardware and other principal hyperparameters are retained in Appendix A.3. Conversely, removing the alternative-loss formula reduces that ablation's reproducibility detail.

R1.justification: v3 adds an explicit relationship to In-Context Pretraining and references supporting similarity sampling, information prioritization, Sentence-BERT and newer model families. References to Phi-1.5 and the pretraining-corpus study by Shin et al. disappear. The central positioning against output-only distillation remains; publication updates to previously cited works are not new research relationships.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and author information, rewrites the ranking-loss discussion, moves implementation details and several analyses into the appendix, and brings limitations into the main text. The impact statement is removed. Most existing prose and the principal section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. Six new experimental tables are added, Table 1 incorporates ± values, and Figure 5 moves to the appendix with a revised vertical scale. Existing case studies are relocated, while the three conceptual diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: The added selector and reverse-KL comparisons, scale sweeps and transfer test strengthen applicability evidence beyond v2. Three-prompt averaging improves reporting, although undefined ± quantities, unspecified prompt variants and removal of the alternative-loss formula limit reproducibility. These provide a limited net improvement over v2's already broad evaluation, independently of higher scores under changed settings.
